stemMd: A researcher randomly assigns 120 volunteers to use either a new study application or their usual method, then compares test-score improvement. Which conclusion is best justified if the application group improves more?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Random assignment supports a causal comparison for these volunteers, but generalization to all students requires care.

options.label: B
options.textMd: The study cannot provide any causal evidence because participants volunteered.

options.label: C
options.textMd: The study proves the application helps every student.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Random assignment makes the volunteers a random sample of all students.

explanationMd: Random assignment helps balance other characteristics between treatment groups and supports causal inference within the study. Volunteer recruitment does not automatically produce a representative sample of the broader student population.

distractorRationale.d: Assignment to treatment is different from population sampling.
distractorRationale.b: Volunteering limits generalization, but random assignment still helps isolate a treatment effect.
distractorRationale.c: An average group effect does not guarantee every individual benefits.
